title: 14th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened with an urgent matter from Dr. Ahmed Shamheed about staffing and service problems at Hulhumale' Hospital; members voted 10 to 37 not to debate it. The main business was the second day of debate on the government's public referendum (consulting the people) bill, sponsored by Ibrahim Falah. Members mostly said they support the bill in principle while raising points about timelines, committee study and unrelated local concerns, and it was accepted 62-0 and sent to the independent institutions committee. The State Owned Enterprises committee report on MMPR Corporation and Maldives Integrated Tourism Development Corporation was then passed 62-0. Attendance counts at the start are partly garbled in the text.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Raised an urgent matter: Hulhumale' Hospital short of doctors and specialists, with outages disrupting services; asked the government to act and the Majlis to debate.
On the referendum bill, said it needed to be matched with the constitution's wording and asked for its fiscal impact to be known before debate.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Welcomed the referendum bill as implementing the constitution's public-consultation provisions and urged the committee to cover how a vote would run in a disaster such as COVID-19.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said the constitution's chapter on rights is locked behind public consultation, suggested a citizen petition route, and asked the committee to study other countries and consult experts.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Called the bill generally good but said the 21-day window for the information paper is too short and should be at least three months; also criticised government delivery of promises.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the bill and proposed that a mid-term secret-ballot vote on the Majlis and an approval vote on the President be considered in committee.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Supported the bill, saying it protects the constitution's rights chapter from being changed without a public vote, and spoke on the supermajority and local concerns in his area.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Supported the bill in principle, citing the change to Addu City's tourism zone without consultation as an example, and favoured committee amendments.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Took the floor and gave up his speaking time.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Called the bill important, explained which constitutional provisions need a public vote, and questioned whether elections should be combined.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said the bill is needed but argued members should first be given real freedom to debate, and criticised how the previous day's debate ended.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: As sponsor, closed the debate, saying the bill lets the public be asked even if the President does not sign, and that committee can fix concerns raised.

decisions: Urgent matter on Hulhumale' Hospital was not accepted for debate (10 for, 37 against).
Public Referendum Bill accepted by the Majlis 62-0 and sent to the independent institutions committee under Rule 106(r).
State Owned Enterprises committee report on MMPR Corporation and Maldives Integrated Tourism Development Corporation passed 62-0.
Next sitting announced for Monday 14 July at 9:00 (year printed as 2024 in the text).
